issue_title: ftest p-values use a different residual degree of freedom than its F statistic
pr_title: Match F-test p-values to the residual degrees of freedom
issue_body:
### Description

`ftest` computes the error mean square using `(M - 1) * (n - 1)` degrees of freedom, but evaluates the F survival function with `(M - 1) * n`. The p-value therefore does not correspond to the F statistic it reports.

```python
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from mlxtend.evaluate import ftest

target = np.ones(4)
first = np.array([1, 1, 1, 0])
second = np.zeros(4)

print(ftest(target, first, second))
print(stats.ttest_rel(first, second))
```

The F statistic is 9, which equals the paired t statistic squared. The original p-value is `0.039941968071718834`; the matching residual degrees of freedom give `0.05766888562243732`, agreeing with the paired t-test. Thus the mismatch can change a decision at 0.05 even though the statistic is unchanged.

### Proposed change and evidence

Use `(M - 1) * (n - 1)` consistently in the F survival function and the user guide. A separate reference fits nested least-squares models with sample and classifier effects, deriving both degrees of freedom from design-matrix ranks.

The same 13 new cases on master `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382` give **12 failed, 1 passed**. The corrected evaluation package gives **167 passed, 2 skipped**. The guide's numerical example still prints the existing rounded result, F=3.873 and p=0.022.

[Successful validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/mlxtend/actions/runs/43667372536). The residual degrees of freedom also follow the within-subject ANOVA decomposition in the [University of Washington worksheet](https://courses.washington.edu/ll317/psych318/files/WSANOVAWorksheet.pdf). [SciPy's paired t-test documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.ttest_rel.html) specifies n - 1 degrees of freedom for the two-model special case.
pr_body:
### Description

The repeated-measures F statistic in `ftest` already uses the residual degrees of freedom `(M - 1) * (n - 1)`, but its p-value uses `(M - 1) * n`. Correct the survival-function argument and the corresponding user-guide formula.

For two models and four examples with correctness vectors `[1, 1, 1, 0]` and `[0, 0, 0, 0]`, F stays 9 while p changes from 0.0399419681 to 0.0576688856. The latter agrees with the equivalent paired t-test (t=3, df=3).

### Validation

Base: `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`. Validated source: `82d02b25ff470232eff19b056c45ff4651ed1c9a`.

- Same 13 new regression/control cases on unchanged production source: **12 failed, 1 passed**.
- Revised evaluation package: **167 passed, 2 skipped**.
- A nested least-squares reference uses sample intercepts and classifier effects, deriving model/residual degrees of freedom from design ranks. It covers 2/3/4 models and 4/6/12 examples.
- Three two-model fixtures compare F with the squared paired t statistic and compare the p-values directly; an equal-accuracy control remains (0, 1).
- Executed the guide's numerical example and verified its rounded F=3.873, p=0.022 output.
- Black, isort and Flake8 pass on changed Python files; checkout cleanliness is verified.
- Python 3.11.18, NumPy 2.4.0, pandas 2.3.3, SciPy 1.16.3 with frozen uv dependencies on Ubuntu. Existing evaluation warnings remain; the full repository suite was not run.

[Successful exact-commit validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/mlxtend/actions/runs/43667372536).

### Related work

Reviewed all-state F-test issues/PRs, including the actual #460 and #1275 diffs. #1275 optimizes object counting and leaves the probability degrees of freedom unchanged. All 34 pre-existing fork branch heads still use the old denominator degrees of freedom.

### Pull Request Checklist

- [x] Added native regression/control tests.
- [x] Corrected the user-guide formula and clarified the public return documentation.
- [x] Relevant tests and changed-file style checks pass.
